<p>Every working woman experiencing the joy of pregnancy also feels concern about her future financial situation. <em>"When should I leave work?", "How much money will I receive?", "Will my workplace wait for me?"</em>.</p><p><strong>Maternity and childbirth leave</strong>, commonly known as "Dekret," is actually a legal right for every working mother. This period is protected by the state so that you can both rest and spend the first months with your baby comfortably.</p><p>In this article, we will set aside the complex language of legislation and explain your rights and the amount you can receive in a simple way.</p><h2>To whom does maternity leave apply?</h2><p>The main condition for receiving maternity leave and payments is having an <strong>official place of employment</strong> and making social insurance (DSMF) payments.</p><ul><li><p><strong>Who can receive it:</strong> Women working under an official employment contract (regardless of whether it is the state or private sector).</p></li><li><p><strong>Who cannot receive it:</strong> Those working unofficially, housewives, or those operating with a VOEN (tax ID) who do not pay social insurance.</p></li></ul><p></p><blockquote><p>Note: If you do not work, you are not eligible for "dekret" money, but a "One-time allowance" of 600 AZN is given to everyone (regardless of whether they work or not).</p></blockquote><p>&gt;</p><h2>How many days can you rest? (Duration)</h2><p>According to the Labor Code of the Republic of Azerbaijan, maternity and childbirth leave is granted for a total of <strong>126 calendar days</strong>:</p><ul><li><p><strong>Before birth:</strong> 70 days (Starts approximately from the 30th week of pregnancy).</p></li><li><p><strong>After birth:</strong> 56 days.</p></li></ul><p><strong>Exceptions:</strong></p><ul><li><p><strong>Difficult birth (Cesarean) or Twins:</strong> If the birth was difficult (e.g., cesarean section) or if two or more children were born, the postpartum leave is extended to <strong>70 days</strong> (Total 140 days).</p></li></ul><h2>How is maternity pay calculated?</h2><p>This is the most interesting part: "How much money will I get?". The payment amount depends on your <strong>official salary</strong> and your <strong>social insurance history</strong>.</p><p>The allowance is paid in the amount of <strong>100%</strong> of your average monthly earnings during the leave period (126 days).</p><p><strong>Simple Calculation Formula:</strong></p><ul><li><p><strong>Average daily earnings:</strong> Divide the sum of official salaries received in the last 12 months by 30.4 (the average number of days in a month). <em>(Roughly speaking, divide your salary by 30)</em>.</p></li><li><p><strong>Final amount:</strong> Multiply the resulting figure by 126 days.</p></li></ul><p><strong>Example:</strong></p><p>Suppose your official salary (gross) is 1000 AZN.</p><ul><li><p>Daily earnings: 1000 / 30.4 ≈ 32.89 AZN</p></li><li><p>Maternity pay: 32.89 x 126 days = <strong>4144 AZN</strong>.</p></li></ul><p></p><blockquote><p>Important: No taxes are deducted from this amount and it is transferred to your card in full.</p></blockquote><p>&gt;</p><h2>Documentation process: What to do?</h2><p>You must follow these steps to go on maternity leave:</p><ul><li><p><strong>Doctor's certificate:</strong> At the 30th week of pregnancy (28th week for twins), you obtain a <strong>"Sick leave certificate" (Bulletin)</strong> from the Women's Consultation Center where you are registered.</p></li><li><p><strong>Submission to workplace:</strong> You present this certificate to the HR (Human Resources) department or accounting of your workplace.</p></li><li><p><strong>Electronic system:</strong> Your workplace enters the information into the electronic system.</p></li><li><p><strong>Payment:</strong> The money is not paid by the employer, but by the <strong>State Social Protection Fund (DSMF)</strong>. The money is transferred directly to your card.</p></li></ul><h2>Is my job protected?</h2><p>Yes! Legislation strictly protects pregnant women and mothers with children up to 3 years old.</p><ul><li><p><strong>Cannot be fired:</strong> The employer cannot fire you during pregnancy or the maternity leave period.</p></li><li><p><strong>Position is held:</strong> You have the right to continue working in the same position and with the same salary upon returning from leave.</p></li></ul><p></p><h2>Partially paid social leave (Childcare)</h2><p>You are not obliged to return to work after the 126-day maternity leave ends. If you wish, you can take "Partially paid social leave" until the child <strong>reaches 3 years of age</strong>.</p><ul><li><p><strong>Amount:</strong> Unfortunately, this amount does not depend on salary and is fixed:</p></li></ul><p>- Until the child reaches 1.5 years: <strong>44 AZN</strong> per month.</p><p>- From 1.5 to 3 years: <strong>28 AZN</strong> per month.</p><ul><li><p>Your workplace is also held for you during this period.</p></li></ul><p></p><p>Maternity leave is not a break given to your career, but time you will devote to the most important "project" of your life – your child. Know your rights and make full use of them.</p><p>To calculate the exact amount you will receive, you can use the <strong>"Maternity Calculator" in the Anacan app</strong>. Just enter your salary, and the app will calculate the rest.</p>
